units.title: Good at + -ing; good and well
notes: be good at + noun or verb-ing: She is good at Geography. He is good at singing.
Negative and questions: I am not good at drawing. Are you good at History?
good is an adjective, well is an adverb: He is a good singer. He sings well.
well goes after the verb and its object: She speaks English well.

items.q: My classmate is very good ___ Geography.
Laura is good at ___ maps.
Our History teacher explains things very ___.
items.why: well tells us how she explains

items.q: Pablo and Ana are ___ students. They always do their homework.
items.why: adjective before a noun, and no plural -s

items.q: ___ you good at Chemistry?
items.why: be good at, so the question uses Are

items.q: I can't run fast, so I ___ good at P.E.
My sister plays the piano ___.
items.why: after a verb and object we use well

items.q: Tom isn't good at ___ early.
My classmate ___.
My brother is good at ___ (swim). He goes to the pool every day.
items.why: good at + verb-ing, and swim doubles the m

items.q: Are you good at ___ (remember) dates in History?
Marta is not very good at ___ (write) stories.
items.why: good at + verb-ing, and write loses the e

items.q: He is a good dancer. He dances very ___ (good).
items.why: the adverb of good is well

items.q: We ___ (be) good at Physics. We always get ten in the exams.
My dad ___ (not/be) good at cooking. His food is terrible!
items.why: my dad is he, so isn't

items.q: I am good in Mathematics.
She is good at sing.
My classmate plays football very good.
a: My classmate plays football very well.
items.why: after a verb we use well

items.q: at / is / good / very / my classmate / drawing
a: My classmate is very good at drawing.

items.q: well / sister / my / does / not / cook
a: My sister does not cook well.

units.title: Question words and forming questions
notes: Question word + do / does + subject + verb: Where does a nurse work?
With be: question word + am / is / are + subject: Who is your teacher?
What time (clock), How many (number), How much (price or amount), How long (time).
Who is for a person, Where a place, When a time, Why a reason, How a way.

items.q: ___ does a nurse work? In a hospital.
___ do firefighters start work? At eight o'clock.
items.why: the answer is a clock time

items.q: ___ astronauts are there in the rocket? Three.
items.why: the answer is a number of people

items.q: ___ is that singer? She is my aunt.
Where ___ the mechanic work?
items.why: the mechanic is he or she, so does

items.q: ___ do you want to be an engineer? Because I like machines.
___ does the film about the artist last? Two hours.
items.why: two hours is a length of time

items.q: What ___ journalists do?
___ does the bandage cost? Two euros.
items.why: How much asks about the price

items.q: Where ___ (do) your father work? He works in a garage.
items.why: your father is he, so does

items.q: What ___ (be) your favourite job?
items.why: your favourite job is it, so is

items.q: What time ___ (the director, start) work every day?
How many hours ___ (do) nurses work every day?
Why ___ (be) firefighters important?
How ___ (you, go) to work every day, Mr Brown?
Where works your mother?
What does an artist does?
items.why: after does the verb has no -s

items.q: How many money does a singer earn?
a: How much money does a singer earn?
items.why: money cannot be counted, so How much

items.q: does / a / what / scientist / do / every day
a: What does a scientist do every day?

items.q: why / the nurse / is / your knee / checking
a: Why is the nurse checking your knee?

units.title: Comparatives and superlatives (short and long adjectives)
notes: Short adjectives: -er than, the -est: Tom is taller than Sam. Ana is the tallest girl in the class.
Long adjectives: more ... than, the most ...: Leo is more confident than me. She is the most serious girl.
Adjectives ending in -y: silly, sillier, the silliest.
Double letter: slim, slimmer. big, bigger. Irregular: good, better, the best.

items.q: My brother is ___ than my dad.
Eva is ___ than her sister. She always helps me.
Marta is ___ confident than her brother.
Carlos is the ___ boy in the class. He plays five sports.
items.why: the + -iest for number one in a group

items.q: This is the ___ building in our town. It is from 2024.
My uncle is ___ than my dad. He has got no hair!
Who is ___ student in your class?
Ana is slim, but her sister is ___.
My dog is sillier ___ my cat.
My grandad is ___ (strong) than my dad. He can lift the sofa!
Lucy is the ___ (silly) girl in our class. She makes everyone laugh.
Our new teacher is ___ (serious) than our old teacher.
Hugo is the ___ (confident) boy in the school play.
My cat is ___ (chubby) than your cat. It eats all day!
Sara is the ___ (good) singer in the class.
items.why: good is irregular: better, the best

items.q: Pablo is more strong than his brother.
a: Pablo is stronger than his brother.

items.q: She is the most kind girl in the school.
a: She is the kindest girl in the school.
She's the kindest girl in the school.

items.q: My sister is taller that me.
a: My sister is taller than me.

items.q: in / is / my family / the / person / sportiest / my mum
a: My mum is the sportiest person in my family.
The sportiest person in my family is my mum.

items.q: more / him / is / than / she / confident
a: She is more confident than him.

units.title: How much and how many
notes: How many + plural nouns you can count: How many coins have you got?
How much + things you cannot count (money, time, water): How much money have you got?
Ask about prices with How much: How much is this wallet? How much are these earrings?
Past questions use did + base verb: How much did it cost? How many presents did you buy?

items.q: How ___ coins are there in your wallet?
items.why: coins can be counted, so many

items.q: How ___ cash have you got?
items.why: cash cannot be counted, so much

items.q: How much ___ the blue rug?
How much ___ the earrings cost?
items.why: earrings is plural, so do ... cost

items.q: How many ___ did you buy?
How much ___ have we got? The shop closes at six.
items.why: How much + a noun you cannot count

items.q: How many notes ___ you spend yesterday?
___ is this wallet? It's twelve pounds.
items.why: How much asks about the price

items.q: How many floors ___ in the department store?
items.why: plural, and question order: are there

items.q: How ___ (much or many) customers are there in the shop?
How ___ (much or many) jewellery does she wear?
How much ___ (be) those earrings in the window?
How much money ___ (you, spend) at the department store yesterday?
items.why: past question: did + subject + base verb

items.q: How many credit cards ___ (have) your dad got?
items.why: your dad is he, so has ... got

items.q: How much ___ (do) this wallet cost?
items.why: this wallet is it, so does

items.q: How many money have you got in your pocket?
a: How much money have you got in your pocket?
items.why: money cannot be counted, so much

items.q: How much coins do you need?
a: How many coins do you need?
items.why: coins can be counted, so many

items.q: How much did the rug costed?
a: How much did the rug cost?

items.q: did / many / buy / how / you / presents
a: How many presents did you buy?
items.why: How many + noun + did + subject + verb

items.q: much / are / earrings / how / the / silver
a: How much are the silver earrings?

units.title: Like, love, enjoy, hate + -ing
notes: like, love, enjoy, hate, don't like + verb-ing: I love surfing. She hates jogging.
he / she / it: likes, loves, enjoys, hates, doesn't like: Tom enjoys playing chess.
Spelling: play, playing. ride, riding (no e). swim, swimming (double letter).
Questions: Do you like hiking? Does she like sailing? Yes, she does.

items.q: I love ___ volleyball on the beach.
My sister ___ jogging in the park.
Tom ___ like playing cricket.
___ you like sailing?
My dad hates ___ up early to go hiking.
items.why: hate + verb-ing, and get doubles the t

items.q: Does Ana like surfing? Yes, she ___.
We enjoy ___ photos of animals.
My friends ___ playing rugby. They play every Saturday.
I ___ wearing a helmet. It's too hot!
My cousin loves ___ (ride) his skateboard in the park.
items.why: love + verb-ing, and ride loses the e

items.q: We enjoy ___ (swim) in the sea in summer.
items.why: enjoy + verb-ing, and swim doubles the m

items.q: My brother ___ (hate) playing chess. He thinks it is boring.
Lucy ___ (not/like) doing karate. She likes tennis.
Do you like ___ (run) in the morning?
items.why: like + verb-ing, and run doubles the n

items.q: My grandad enjoys ___ (do) tai chi every morning.
I like play hockey with my friends.
a: I like playing hockey with my friends.
I like to play hockey with my friends.

items.q: She enjoy hiking in the mountains.
a: She enjoys hiking in the mountains.

items.q: My brother hates runing.
on / loves / my / Saturdays / playing / sister / tennis
a: My sister loves playing tennis on Saturdays.
On Saturdays my sister loves playing tennis.
On Saturdays, my sister loves playing tennis.

items.q: like / brother / does / skateboarding / your

units.title: Advice and orders: should, must and imperatives
notes: should / shouldn't + verb for advice: You should tidy up your room. You shouldn't eat on the armchair.
must / mustn't + verb for rules and orders: You must do the dishes. You mustn't touch the stove.
No to and no -s after should and must: He should help (not should to help, not shoulds help).
Imperatives give orders: Sweep the floor, please. Don't open the oven.

items.q: You ___ touch the stove. It's very hot!
items.why: mustn't means do not do it

items.q: Your room is very untidy. You ___ tidy up.
items.why: should means it is a good idea

items.q: You should ___ the plants. They are very dry.
___ out the rubbish, please. The bin is full.
___ put your feet on the armchair!
My brother ___ help with the laundry.
We ___ play football in the living room. Mum gets angry.
items.why: it is a bad idea, so shouldn't

items.q: It's a rule in our house. Everybody ___ do the dishes after dinner.
___ clean the mirror now? Yes, please.
You ___ (must, not) open the washing machine when it is on.
It's very late. You ___ (should, not) watch TV now.
Dad should ___ (clean) the toilet today. It's his turn.
Please ___ (not/leave) your clothes on the floor.
Mum says we must ___ (put away) the clothes before dinner.
Your sister must ___ (be) careful with the oven.
You should to do the dishes.
He musts take out the rubbish.
a: He must take out the rubbish.

items.q: Not open the refrigerator!
the / you / floor / should / sweep / every day
a: You should sweep the floor every day.
Every day you should sweep the floor.
Every day, you should sweep the floor.

items.q: mustn't / the curtains / you / with / play
a: You mustn't play with the curtains.

units.title: Play, do and go with sports and activities
notes: play + ball sports and games: play volleyball, play chess.
go + activities ending in -ing: go sailing, go camping, go hiking.
do + other activities without a ball: do karate, do yoga, do gymnastics.
Past forms: played, went, did: Last summer we went canoeing.

items.q: We ___ volleyball on the beach every summer.
My family ___ camping every August.
My mum ___ yoga on Mondays.
Last summer we ___ canoeing on the river.
items.why: go canoeing, and the past of go is went

items.q: Did you ___ surfing last weekend?
items.why: Did + base verb, and go surfing

items.q: My friends ___ gymnastics after school.
Let's go ___ in the mountains. Bring your hiking boots!
Yesterday Tom ___ tennis with his cousin at the campsite.
items.why: play tennis, in the past played

items.q: She doesn't ___ sailing in winter. It's too cold.
items.why: doesn't + base verb, and go sailing

items.q: Last August we ___ (go) camping and slept in sleeping bags.
items.why: last August is past, so went

items.q: My sister ___ (do) gymnastics every Tuesday.
Look! The children ___ (play) volleyball on the beach now.
We ___ (not/go) hiking yesterday because it rained.
My dad loves going ___ (cycle) at the weekend.
items.why: go + verb-ing, and cycle loses the e

items.q: I ___ (play) chess with my grandad every Sunday.
items.why: every Sunday is a habit, and I has no -s

items.q: I play karate on Fridays.
items.why: karate has no ball, so do karate

items.q: We go to camping every summer.
Yesterday we go canoeing on the lake.
a: Yesterday we went canoeing on the lake.

items.q: go / we / with / every / hiking / summer / our cousins
a: We go hiking with our cousins every summer.
Every summer we go hiking with our cousins.
Every summer, we go hiking with our cousins.
We go hiking every summer with our cousins.

items.q: you / did / camping / go / last / weekend
a: Did you go camping last weekend?

units.title: Future with will and won't
notes: will + verb for the future and for what we think will happen: I think it will be a fantastic day.
Short form 'll: I'll, you'll, she'll, we'll, they'll. Negative: won't (will not).
will is the same for everybody, and the verb has no to and no -s: She will come.
Questions: Will you be at the party? Yes, I will. No, I won't.

items.q: I think Anna ___ her present.
items.why: will + base verb, no -s and no to

items.q: Don't worry. The test ___ be difficult.
___ you come to my party tomorrow?
items.why: tomorrow, so the question uses Will

items.q: My brother ___ ten next month.
items.why: age uses be, and will never takes -s

items.q: Will they be angry? No, they ___.
items.why: short answer repeats will or won't

items.q: It's very cold. I think it ___ tomorrow.
Wait here. ___ be back in five minutes.
items.why: I'll is the short form of I will

items.q: Where ___ you be at six o'clock tomorrow?
Tom is ill. He ___ to school tomorrow.
I'm thirsty. I think I ___ (drink) some water in a minute.
Don't be frightened. The dog ___ (not/hurt) you.
Next year we ___ (be) in Year 5.
items.why: next year is future: will be

items.q: I'm sure you ___ (feel) fantastic after the holidays.
One day people will live on the moon, but they ___ (not/live) on the sun!
Will your parents ___ (be) proud of you? Yes, they will.
She will to be excited tomorrow.
They don't will come to the party.
a: They won't come to the party.
They will not come to the party.

items.q: Will be you at home tonight?
a: Will you be at home tonight?

items.q: my mum / will / I think / very proud / be
a: I think my mum will be very proud.

items.q: will / where / be / you / next summer
a: Where will you be next summer?

units.title: Present perfect with ever and never
notes: have / has + past participle: I have visited a museum. She has travelled by rocket.
Have you ever...? asks about your life: Have you ever seen a rocket?
never means not in my life: I have never been to space (not I haven't never been).
Short answers: Yes, I have. No, he hasn't.

items.q: ___ a shooting star?
I have ___ been to space.
items.why: never in positive sentences, ever in questions

items.q: My sister ___ never seen a spaceship.
Have you ever ___ a planet through a telescope?
items.why: past participle of see is seen

items.q: Has the explorer ever found a space rock? No, he ___.
We ___ never travelled by rocket.
___ your dad ever been on a plane?
items.why: your dad is he, so Has

items.q: I ___ touched a rock from the moon. I want to touch one!
items.why: never goes with a positive verb

items.q: Have they ever visited Earth? Yes, they ___.
I have never ___ (travel) in a spaceship.
Have you ever ___ (be) to a space museum?
items.why: past participle of be is been

items.q: My grandad has never ___ (see) the Earth from a plane.
items.why: past participle of see is seen

items.q: She ___ (never/visit) another planet, but she wants to be an astronaut.
Has your teacher ever ___ (study) the planets?
We ___ (never/walk) on the moon.
I haven't never seen a rocket.
a: I have never seen a rocket.
I haven't ever seen a rocket.
items.why: never goes with a positive verb

items.q: Have you ever see a spaceship?
a: Have you ever seen a spaceship?
items.why: we need the past participle seen

items.q: He have never visited another planet.
a: He has never visited another planet.

items.q: ever / you / a / have / touched / space rock
a: Have you ever touched a space rock?

items.q: has / my / never / seen / a rocket / brother
a: My brother has never seen a rocket.
items.why: never goes between has and the past participle
